context.title: Apollo 1, 1967
context.text: On 27 January 1967 three astronauts lost their lives when a fire swept through the Apollo 1 command module during a preflight test. NASA's review found that the pure oxygen atmosphere let the fire spread quickly, and NASA then restricted combustible materials in the spacecraft and replaced the hatch with one that opens in three seconds.
context.sourceName: NASA Office of Safety and Mission Assurance, Apollo 1

context.title: Apollo 13, 1970
context.text: On the third day of the mission, oxygen tank number two blew up, which led to the failure of tank number one and ended the plan to land on the Moon. For later missions engineers redesigned the oxygen tank system and sheathed all electrical wiring in stainless steel.
context.sourceName: NASA Office of Safety and Mission Assurance, Apollo 13

context.title: Fire aboard Mir, 1997
context.text: On 24 February 1997 a fire ignited in an oxygen generating system aboard the space station Mir, with six crew members aboard. The flame lasted several minutes, cut off access to one of the two Soyuz escape vehicles and filled the modules with smoke before the crew put it out.
context.sourceName: NASA History, 25 Years Ago: Fire Aboard Space Station Mir

context.title: Lighter air tanks for firefighters
context.text: NASA's Johnson Space Center and Scott Aviation developed lightweight air tanks for firefighters. The backpack system weighs 20 pounds for a 30 minute air supply, which is 13 pounds less than conventional firefighting tanks.

context.title: A detector that tells smoke from dust
context.text: A fire detector first used in space shuttle orbiters samples the air for combustion particles and can tell them apart from other matter such as dust. That makes it less susceptible to false alarms.

context.title: Better protective gear for firefighters
context.text: Project FIRES, sponsored by NASA and the U.S. Fire Administration, applied lightweight, fire-resistant and heat-protective materials first developed for astronauts' space suits to firefighter gear. Its goal was to curb injuries and fatalities among firefighters.
context.sourceName: NASA Spinoff, New Technology for the Fire Attire
